examples.ko: 시험에서 일등을 한 뒤로 그 친구는 기고만장해요.
examples.en: Ever since he came first on the exam, that friend has been full of himself.
Don't get too cocky just because you were praised a little.

examples.ko: 승진하고 나서 기고만장한 모습이 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: He looks cocky since his promotion, and it's not a good look.

examples.ko: 형은 한 번 이기면 금방 기고만장해져요.
examples.en: My older brother gets cocky as soon as he wins once.
The person who was so full of himself is quiet these days.
I was talking all puffed up and ended up making a mistake.

explain: 잘난 척하고 우쭐대는 부정적인 느낌이 강해서, 보통 다른 사람을 보며 '너무 기고만장하다'고 말해요. '기세등등하다'와 비슷하지만 '기고만장하다'가 더 잘난 척하는 느낌이에요. '기고만장해지다'처럼 변화를 나타내는 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It carries a negative feeling of showing off and getting cocky, so people usually say it about someone else. It is close to '기세등등하다', but '기고만장하다' feels more arrogant. You can also use it for change, as in '기고만장해지다' (to become cocky).

examples.en: The groundbreaking ceremony for the new hospital is held tomorrow.
The mayor also attended the apartment groundbreaking ceremony.

examples.ko: 기공식 날에는 비가 와서 행사가 조금 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: It rained on the day of the groundbreaking, so the event was a bit late.
I saw the bridge construction groundbreaking ceremony on the news.
I took a photo of them digging the first shovel at the groundbreaking.

examples.ko: 공장 기공식은 다음 달 초로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: The factory groundbreaking has been set for early next month.

explain: 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사이고, 반대로 공사가 끝났을 때 하는 행사는 '준공식'이에요. 비슷한 말로 '착공식'도 써요. 보통 '기공식을 열다/하다', '기공식에 참석하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: This is the event held when construction starts; the one held when it finishes is '준공식'. '착공식' is a similar word. People usually say '기공식을 열다/하다' or '기공식에 참석하다'.

examples.en: The long winter has finally ended.

examples.ko: 이 길은 기나길어서 걸어가면 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: This road is so long that it takes about an hour on foot.
The summer vacation felt long and boring.

examples.ko: 그는 기나긴 재판 끝에 무죄를 받았어요.
examples.en: After a very long trial, he was found not guilty.

examples.ko: 기나길었던 시간이 지나고 이제 봄이 왔어요.
examples.en: The long stretch of time has passed and spring has come.
The waiting time felt endlessly long.

explain: '길다'보다 시간이나 길이가 지루할 만큼 아주 길다는 느낌이 강해요. '기나긴 밤'처럼 'ㄴ' 앞에서는 'ㄹ'이 빠지고, '기나길어요'처럼 다른 때는 그대로예요. '기나긴 겨울'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 꼴이 글에서 잘 보여요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '길다', suggesting something is tiresomely long in time or distance. The 'ㄹ' drops before 'ㄴ', as in '기나긴 밤', but stays elsewhere, as in '기나길어요'. The modifier form, as in '기나긴 겨울', is easy to find in writing.

examples.en: The CEO gave the founding anniversary speech.
The commemorative speech was so long that it got a bit boring.
In the commemorative address, the president thanked the employees.

examples.ko: 졸업 기념사는 오 분 안에 끝났어요.
examples.en: The graduation address ended within five minutes.
What will be included in this commemorative address?

examples.ko: 기념사 원고를 쓰느라 어젯밤 늦게 잤어요.
examples.en: I went to bed late last night writing the speech draft.

explain: 기념일이나 기념행사에서 하는 연설이에요. 축하하는 말은 '축사', 맞이하는 말은 '환영사'처럼 행사에서 하는 말마다 이름이 달라요. '기념사를 하다/발표하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is a speech given on an anniversary or at a commemorative event. Other event speeches have their own names, such as '축사' (congratulatory) and '환영사' (welcome). People say '기념사를 하다/발표하다'.

examples.en: A commemorative coin came out to mark the Olympics.
I received a commemorative coin as a gift from my grandfather.

examples.ko: 기념주화는 일반 동전과 달리 모양이 특별해요.
examples.en: Unlike ordinary coins, commemorative coins have special designs.
I stood in line at the bank to buy a commemorative coin.
The tournament logo is engraved on the commemorative coin.
My friend collects commemorative coins as a hobby.

explain: 행사나 사건을 기념하려고 특별하게 만든 동전이에요. 뉴스에서는 '기념주화를 발행하다'라고 하고, 일상에서는 쉽게 '기념 동전'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a coin specially made to mark an event or occasion. In the news you will hear '기념주화를 발행하다' (to issue a commemorative coin), and in daily talk people also say '기념 동전'.

examples.en: That player is our team's rising star.

examples.ko: 신인 기대주로 불리던 가수가 상을 탔어요.
examples.en: The singer who was called a promising newcomer won an award.
Let me introduce this year's most promising talent.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어릴 때부터 수영 기대주였어요.
examples.en: That kid has been a swimming prospect since childhood.
The up-and-coming players are gathered and practicing hard.

examples.ko: 기대주 한 명이 마침내 첫 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: One of the promising young players finally scored his first goal.

explain: '유망주'와 비슷하게 앞으로 잘할 거라고 기대받는 사람에게 써요. 스포츠나 연예계의 신인 이야기에서 자주 들려요. '기대주'는 사람에게 쓰고 물건에는 '기대작'처럼 다른 말을 써요.
explain_en: Like '유망주', it is used for a person expected to do well in the future, and you often hear it about newcomers in sports or entertainment. '기대주' is for people; for works or products a different word such as '기대작' is used.

examples.en: Motorcycles are agile, so they are convenient for deliveries.
This team beat its opponent with its quick mobility.

examples.ko: 소방차의 기동력을 높이려면 길을 비켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please make way to help fire trucks move quickly.

examples.ko: 작은 회사의 기동력은 큰 회사보다 나아요.
examples.en: A small company's agility is better than a big company's.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 기동력 있는 선수가 필요해요.
examples.en: Our team needs a mobile, quick player.

examples.ko: 눈이 와서 구급차의 기동력에 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because of the snow, the ambulance had trouble getting around.

explain: '기동성'과 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 차, 소방, 경찰, 스포츠, 회사 일처럼 상황에 맞게 빠르게 움직이는 이야기에 나와요.
explain_en: It is often interchangeable with '기동성'. It appears in talk about moving quickly as needed, such as cars, fire services, police, sports and company work.

examples.en: This car is small, so it is easy to maneuver.
I cut down my luggage to be more mobile.

examples.ko: 기동성 때문에 사람들이 스쿠터를 많이 타요.
examples.en: People ride scooters a lot because of their mobility.
Laptops are portable, but the screen is small.
At the site, safety comes before mobility.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 가벼워서 기동성에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This bag is light, so it helps with getting around.

explain: '기동력'과 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 차, 가방, 노트북처럼 가볍고 움직이기 편한 것을 말할 때도 나와요. '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is close to '기동력' and the two are often swapped. It also comes up for things that are light and easy to move, like cars, bags and laptops. People say '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'.

examples.en: It is not easy to give up your vested interests.
He is a young politician who challenges the establishment.
When the establishment came up, the debate heated up.

examples.ko: 기득권이 있는 사람들이 법 개정에 반대했어요.
examples.en: People with vested interests opposed the revision of the law.

examples.ko: 기득권 싸움 때문에 일이 자꾸 늦어져요.
examples.en: Because of the fight over vested interests, things keep getting delayed.
I want to give up my vested position and start anew.

explain: 이미 가지고 있는 권리나 이익을 말하는데, 뉴스에서는 '기득권을 지키다/내려놓다'처럼 변화를 막는 쪽의 이야기로 많이 나와요. 이미 힘이 있는 집단은 '기득권층'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to rights or benefits someone already holds, and in the news it often comes up on the side resisting change, as in '기득권을 지키다/내려놓다'. A group that already holds power is called '기득권층'.

examples.ko: 그 대회에는 기라성 같은 선수들이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A galaxy of star players took part in that tournament.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 선배들 사이에서 발표하려니 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was nervous presenting among such a star-studded group of seniors.

examples.ko: 이 학교에서는 기라성 같은 작가들이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A host of famous writers came out of this school.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 인물들 중에서도 그분이 제일 유명해요.
examples.en: Even among such stars, that person is the most famous.

examples.ko: 영화에는 기라성 같은 배우들이 줄줄이 나와요.
examples.en: One famous actor after another appears in the film.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 대학 동기들이 지금은 각 분야에서 활약해요.
examples.en: My star-studded college classmates are now active in their own fields.

explain: 거의 '기라성 같은'의 꼴로 쓰고, 뛰어난 사람이 여럿 모여 있을 때 말해요. 사람 한 명보다는 여러 명을 가리킬 때 자연스러워요. 주로 글이나 방송에서 보여요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '기라성 같은', when many outstanding people are gathered. It sounds natural for a group rather than a single person. You mostly see it in writing and broadcasts.

examples.en: The door creaked, so I oiled the hinges.

examples.ko: 자전거 체인에 기름칠하면 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: If you oil the bicycle chain, it stops making noise.
My father oils his tools every weekend.

examples.ko: 기름칠해 둔 덕분에 기계가 잘 돌아가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the oiling, the machine runs well.
I learned how to oil it from a video.
Oil it in advance before it rusts.

explain: 기계나 문의 움직이는 부분에 기름을 바른다는 말인데, '기름을 치다'라고도 많이 해요. 기계의 녹을 막거나 소리를 없앨 때 써요.
explain_en: You apply oil to moving parts of machines or doors, and people also say '기름을 치다'. It is used to prevent rust or stop squeaking.

examples.ko: 이 서류는 기밀문서라서 복사하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This is a classified document, so you must not copy it.

examples.ko: 회사 기밀문서를 밖으로 가져가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take the company's confidential documents outside.
Confidential documents are kept in a locked drawer.
Confidential documents were leaked and it was on the news.

examples.ko: 기밀문서에 접근할 수 있는 사람은 몇 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only a few people can access the confidential documents.

examples.ko: 기밀문서로 분류된 자료는 이메일로 보내지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not send materials classified as confidential by email.

explain: 밖으로 알려지면 안 되는 중요한 서류를 말해요. '기밀문서를 유출하다', '기밀문서로 분류되다'처럼 쓰고, 일상에서는 '비밀 서류'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to important papers that must not become public. People say '기밀문서를 유출하다' (to leak) or '기밀문서로 분류되다' (to be classified), and in daily talk also '비밀 서류'.

examples.en: It was a presentation that showed the new employee's spirit.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 기백을 잃지 않고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to keep my spirit even as I get older.
A spirited young man stepped forward.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 기백에 눌려서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was overwhelmed by his spirit and couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 기백으로 가득한 응원 소리가 경기장에 울렸어요.
examples.en: Cheers full of spirit rang through the stadium.

examples.ko: 목소리는 작아도 기백만은 누구한테도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if my voice is small, I'm second to none in spirit.

explain: '패기'와 비슷하게 굽히지 않는 씩씩한 마음과 태도를 말해요. '기백이 있다/넘치다'처럼 쓰고, 목소리나 표정에서 느껴지는 힘을 칭찬할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: Like '패기', it means a bold, unyielding spirit and attitude. People say '기백이 있다/넘치다', and it suits praise for strength felt in a voice or expression.

examples.ko: 시골에 계신 부모님께 도착했다고 기별을 드렸어요.
examples.en: I sent word to my parents in the countryside that I had arrived.

examples.ko: 거래처에서는 일주일이 지나도록 아무 기별이 없어요.
examples.en: There has been no word from the client even after a week.

examples.ko: 도착하면 꼭 저한테 먼저 기별해 주세요.
examples.en: When you arrive, please let me know first.

examples.ko: 친구가 이사를 가면서 새 주소를 기별했어요.
examples.en: My friend sent word of the new address when moving.
The person in charge will let you know soon.
A friend from my hometown came without any notice.

explain: 요즘 일상에서는 '연락하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '기별'은 조금 옛스럽고 정감 있게 들려요. '기별이 오다/없다', '기별을 드리다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: In daily life '연락하다' is more common today, and '기별' sounds a little old-fashioned and warm. It is often used in pairs like '기별이 오다/없다' and '기별을 드리다'.

examples.en: The constitution guarantees the basic rights of citizens.

examples.ko: 모든 사람은 교육을 받을 기본권이 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has the basic right to receive an education.
We debated the issue of violations of basic rights.
Freedom of expression is also included in basic rights.

examples.ko: 아이들의 기본권은 어른들이 함께 지켜 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Adults must work together to protect children's basic rights.
It took a long time for it to be recognized as a basic right.

explain: 헌법이 보장하는 국민의 중요한 권리를 말할 때 써요. 뉴스와 사회 수업에서 '기본권을 보장하다/침해하다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for the important rights that the constitution guarantees to citizens. In the news and social studies class it often appears as '기본권을 보장하다/침해하다'.

examples.en: We came back from the brink late in the game and won.
That company was revived thanks to its new product.

examples.ko: 큰 수술을 받고 기사회생한 환자가 퇴원했어요.
examples.en: The patient who came back from the brink after major surgery was discharged.
The team changed its strategy in order to make a comeback.
We need a way to recover from this crisis.
Everyone had given up, so it's hard to believe it came back to life.

explain: 거의 죽을 뻔하거나 망할 뻔했다가 다시 살아날 때 써요. 사람의 건강뿐 아니라 경기, 회사 이야기에도 많이 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '되살아나다'가 있고, 일상 대화에서는 그쪽이 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is used when someone or something nearly died or failed and then came back. It appears not only for health but also for games and companies. A similar word is '되살아나다', which is easier in everyday talk.

examples.en: That person's ideas are truly out of this world.
Many wildly inventive devices are on display.
The story is so far-fetched that it's hard to believe.
A wildly unusual-looking building is the talk of the town.

examples.ko: 기상천외했던 그날의 일을 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the incredible events of that day.
I didn't know it would be this extraordinary.

explain: 보통 사람이 생각하기 어려울 만큼 특이하고 놀랍다는 느낌이에요. 아이디어, 방법, 이야기처럼 생각해 낸 것에 잘 어울려요. '황당하다'와 달리 신기하다는 감탄이 들어가기도 해요.
explain_en: It suggests something so unusual and surprising that an ordinary person would hardly think of it. It suits ideas, methods and stories. Unlike '황당하다', it can carry a note of amazement.

examples.en: I want to major in meteorology at university.
I learned the types of clouds in meteorology class.
Meteorologists are analyzing the typhoon's path.
Meteorology gets more interesting the more you study it.

examples.ko: 기상학에 관심이 생겨서 관련 책을 샀어요.
examples.en: I became interested in meteorology and bought a related book.

examples.ko: 기상학적으로 보면 올해 여름은 유난히 더웠어요.
examples.en: Meteorologically speaking, this summer was unusually hot.

explain: '기상 예보'의 '기상'은 날씨를 뜻하고, '기상 시간'의 '기상'은 잠에서 일어나는 것이라 서로 달라요. 일상에서는 '날씨'라고 쉽게 말하고, '기상학'은 수업이나 학문 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: The '기상' in '기상 예보' refers to weather, while the '기상' in '기상 시간' means waking up, so they are different words. In daily life people just say '날씨', and '기상학' appears in classes and academic talk.

examples.en: A tailored suit is expensive, so I bought a ready-made one.

examples.ko: 기성품은 사이즈가 맞는지 입어 봐야 해요.
examples.en: With ready-made clothes, you have to try them on to check the size.

examples.ko: 이 가구는 기성품이라 바로 가져갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: This furniture is ready-made, so you can take it right away.

examples.ko: 기성품 말고 직접 만든 선물을 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give a handmade gift, not something store-bought.
I found a pretty enough outfit even among ready-made ones.

examples.ko: 기성품이 아니라서 주문하면 한 달쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It's not ready-made, so an order takes about a month.

explain: 미리 만들어 놓고 파는 물건이라서 주문 제작이나 맞춤과 반대되는 말이에요. 옷은 '기성복'이라고 해요. '기성품을 사다'처럼 쓰고, 맞춤은 '맞춤 제작'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: These are goods made in advance and sold, so it is the opposite of custom-made or tailored. Clothes are called '기성복'. People say '기성품을 사다', and tailor-made is '맞춤 제작'.

examples.en: The players on the winning team are full of confidence.
That person who had been so full of vigor suddenly got quiet.
He walked into the meeting room with a swaggering look.
When they took the lead, the opposing team became cocky.
He boasted loudly and confidently, but ended up making a mistake.
At first he was full of vigor, but soon he lost heart.

explain: 기운이 대단하고 당당한 모습을 말해요. '기고만장하다'와 비슷하지만 '기고만장하다'가 잘난 척하는 느낌이 더 강해요. 승리하거나 힘이 생겼을 때 사람이나 팀에게 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes an imposing, confident energy. It is similar to '기고만장하다', but that word feels more like showing off. It is often used for a person or team that has won or gained power.

examples.en: The prosecution submitted the indictment to the court.

examples.ko: 기소장에는 혐의 내용이 자세히 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The details of the charges are written out in the indictment.
People were shocked when the indictment was made public.
The news reported part of the indictment's contents.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 기소장은 열 쪽이 넘어요.
examples.en: The indictment in this case is over ten pages long.
An indictment and a court ruling are different documents.

explain: 검사가 재판을 청구할 때 법원에 내는 서류예요. '기소장을 제출하다'처럼 쓰고, 판결이 적힌 서류는 '판결문'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is the document a prosecutor submits to the court when requesting a trial. You say '기소장을 제출하다', and the paper with the verdict is called '판결문', which is different. It appears often in news and legal talk.

examples.en: The road was blocked by a sudden downpour.
I was surprised when the company raised prices all of a sudden.
It was a surprise announcement, so there was no time to prepare.
It was so sudden that it was hard to respond.
Even when asked a surprise question, I answered calmly.
Citizens were startled by the policy announced out of the blue.

explain: 관형사로 분류되지만 실제로는 '기습적인', '기습적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요. '갑자기'와 달리 상대가 준비하지 못한 때에 하는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '기습적 인상', '기습적 폭우' 같은 말로 보여요.
explain_en: Although it is classified as a determiner, it is actually used with endings like '기습적인' and '기습적으로'. Unlike '갑자기', it implies doing something when the other side is unprepared. In the news you see phrases like '기습적 인상' (a surprise hike) and '기습적 폭우'.
